The team

The team by department

Each band is a domain chapter of the book. People set intent and own outcomes. Agents do the work inside limits people control.

Showing all 76 agents and 10 human roles in 11 departments.

Finance: record-to-report

10 agents

The close: journals, reconciliations, accruals, intercompany, consolidation and reporting. Book, Ch 12

  • Close orchestrator agent Runs the close calendar across entities. It monitors entity close progress and sequences the close tasks other agents and people perform. L3–L4 3 tasks Ch 12.3.1
  • Journal agent Maps a journal request to a known pattern. It reads source data, builds the entry with support and submits it to the ledger’s own checks. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 12.5.2
  • Journal verification agent Reads entries that people or other processes posted. It flags unusual ones with evidence. L3 4 tasks Ch 12.5.2
  • Clearing agent Matches open items with fuzzy references and many-to-many grouping. A confidence score drives whether it clears, proposes or routes. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 12.6.2
  • GR/IR agent Classifies each open goods-receipt and invoice-receipt line by root cause. It proposes the fix for each cause. L2–L3 6 tasks Ch 12.6.3
  • Account certification agent Certifies account balances in three risk tiers. It attaches evidence and drafts variance explanations from posting history. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 12.6.4
  • Accrual agent Finds accrual candidates, estimates amounts and applies the written policy. It proposes the batch with method, data and policy reference per line. L1–L2 5 tasks Ch 12.7.1
  • Intercompany agent Matches intercompany items across ledgers. It classifies why a difference exists and proposes which side corrects with what entry. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 12.8
  • Consolidation validation agent Runs validations continuously against integrated data. It explains each failure in business terms and sends the proposed correction to the named person. L2–L3 3 tasks Ch 12.9.2
  • Commentary agent Drafts flux commentary and recurring notes around ledger figures. Each claim cites the query that produced its number. L2–L4 4 tasks Ch 12.9.3

Finance: cash, payables and treasury

10 agents

Billing, credit, cash application, collections, disputes, invoices, payments and the cash forecast. Book, Ch 13

  • Billing anomaly gate agent Scores each draft invoice against the customer’s history before it is sent. Invoices above the threshold go to a hold queue with an explanation. L3 2 tasks Ch 13.4.1
  • Credit block resolution agent Handles the outputs of the deterministic credit engine. It writes a score and a decision; a deterministic credit rule releases the block. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 13.4.2
  • Cash application agent Matches incoming payments to open items. The ledger clears automatically on the agent’s match above a threshold the controller sets. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 13.5.2
  • Collections prioritization agent Ranks open items by where an action changes the payment date. It applies the treatment matrix and gives collectors a brief, not a decision. L1–L4 5 tasks Ch 13.6.3
  • Dispute intake agent Opens and classifies the customer’s dispute case. It assigns reason codes from the customer’s message and calls the dispute validation agent. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 13.7.3
  • Dispute validation and credit agent Checks the open item, terms, proof of delivery and price agreement across systems. It proposes an outcome; the policy table decides who approves. L2–L3 4 tasks Ch 13.7.4
  • Invoice capture and match exception agent Captures supplier invoices and works match exceptions. It releases variance blocks within limits; the ledger’s rules post the invoice. L3 4 tasks Ch 13.9.3
  • Payment proposal agent Builds the payment proposal or batch up to the last step. A person or separate system approves the release before money moves. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 13.10.1
  • Payment scheduling agent Compares each invoice’s annualized discount rate with treasury’s daily hurdle rate. It schedules invoices for the discount date or net due date. L3 2 tasks Ch 13.11.2
  • Cash positioning and forecast agent Builds the daily cash position and 13-week forecast. It proposes transfers and hedges for people to approve. L1–L4 8 tasks Ch 13.12.1

Procurement and spend

10 agents

Source-to-pay: spend data, intake, PO approval, sourcing, contracts and supplier risk. Book, Ch 14

  • Spend classification agent Classifies spend into one category taxonomy across ledgers, cards and expenses. It builds the spend cube every spend agent reads. L2–L4 3 tasks Ch 14.5.2
  • Intake agent Reads incoming purchase requests and routes each to the right channel. It does not commit money. L3 4 tasks Ch 14.6.2
  • PO approval agent Predicts with a calibrated probability whether the approver would approve. It acts only where that clears the threshold p* = L / (G + L). L2–L3 4 tasks Ch 14.6.3
  • Sourcing agent Prepares and runs sourcing events by type. It ranks bids on total cost of ownership and awards only tail spot buys. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 14.7.2
  • Negotiation agent Negotiates only inside an envelope a person approves before the first counteroffer. Every message says "subject to approval". Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 14.7.5
  • Contract agent Drafts, reviews and monitors supplier contracts against the clause playbook. It turns signed terms into records for people to confirm. L2–L4 4 tasks Ch 14.8.1
  • Renewal agent Prevents silent auto-renewals on a 120/90/60/30-day cadence. It decides nothing; it makes sure a person decides in time. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 14.8.4
  • Supplier risk agent Computes and explains a five-dimension supplier risk score. It blocks new POs on a sanctions hit and prepares options for supplier distress. L1–L4 5 tasks Ch 14.9.2
  • Payment-terms validation agent Compares payment terms on the PO, contract and supplier master. It corrects them to the contract or playbook value and logs the change. L3 2 tasks Ch 14.10.4
  • Payments fraud document agent Analyzes supplier bank letters and change requests for manipulation before an account is activated. It is a filter, not the control. L2 2 tasks Ch 14.9.4

Supply chain and manufacturing

6 agents

Planning, suppliers, maintenance, warehouse and quality, with physical AI behind the OT boundary. Book, Ch 15

  • Exception coordinator agent Owns one cross-domain event from open to close. Domain agents contribute analysis; it prices the impact and routes decisions to named approvers. L2–L3 5 tasks Ch 15.2.1
  • Supplier agent Turns supplier emails and PDFs into structured change requests. It matches each to the purchase orders it affects. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 15.3.2
  • Planning agent Groups exception messages into issues with causes. It runs the planning engine’s own simulation of options; solvers still compute the plan. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 15.3.1
  • Maintenance agent Turns condition alerts into work orders and inspection plans into robot missions. It reorders spare parts by asset criticality. L2–L4 6 tasks Ch 15.5.1
  • Warehouse agent Reads physical events from robots and cameras. It decides what each means for stock and tasks, then writes back to the owning system. L2–L3 5 tasks Ch 15.8.2
  • Quality agent Proposes vision-inspection threshold changes weekly from production results and warranty claims. A quality engineer approves every change. L2 1 task Ch 15.11.3

Front office: sales, service and marketing

5 agents

Sales, quotes, customer service, voice, field service and marketing. Book, Ch 16

  • Sales agent Researches accounts, qualifies leads and keeps the pipeline clean. It drafts quotes inside price bands and forecast notes the sales leader owns. L1–L4 11 tasks Ch 16.3.1
  • Customer service agent Answers and acts on standard cases end to end within limits. It prepares summaries and evidence for specialists on complex cases. L1–L4 6 tasks Ch 16.5.1
  • Voice agent Handles customer calls by voice. It discloses the AI in the first sentence and hands over to a human with the full transcript. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 16.5.4
  • Field service agent Turns a service case into a diagnosis, a scheduled visit and a reserved part. It drafts the service report and invoice for the technician. L2–L4 6 tasks Ch 16.5.6
  • Marketing and campaign agent Builds segments from consented data and drafts variants from approved claims. It shifts campaign spend inside a band, not a budget. L2–L3 6 tasks Ch 16.6.1

People and HR

8 agents

Agents organize work about people. Evaluating a person stays with a named human. Book, Ch 16

  • Recruiting agent Organizes hiring: requisitions, ads, applications, scheduling and offers. It shows no score; people evaluate candidates. L0–L3 7 tasks Ch 16.7.3
  • Onboarding coordinator agent Owns the new-hire case from offer acceptance to day 30. It removes delays at hand-offs across HR, IT, facilities and payroll. L2–L3 7 tasks Ch 16.8.1
  • HR service agent Answers employee questions from policy and personal HR data. It handles standard transactions such as employment letters. L3–L4 3 tasks Ch 16.9.1
  • Payroll variance agent Checks every payslip before release. It closes flags with a documented known cause and passes the rest to a payroll specialist. Level not stated 2 tasks Ch 16.9.2
  • Time and shift agent Explains time exceptions and confirms shift swaps by published rules. A solver drafts the rota; the supervisor publishes it. L2–L3 4 tasks Ch 16.9.4
  • Compensation agent Prepares merit budgets and pay grids and flags out-of-grid proposals. It runs pay-equity analysis for the committee. L3 3 tasks Ch 16.11.3
  • Performance calibration agent Builds evidence packs and shows rating distributions with names hidden. It never proposes a rating. L0–L1 3 tasks Ch 16.11.2
  • Workforce planning agent Models build, buy, borrow and automate scenarios from skills data and business demand. It is a planning tool for HR and finance. L1–L2 1 task Ch 16.11.1

IT and shared services

7 agents

Service desk, access, incidents, change, batch operations, releases and the employee front door. Book, Ch 17

  • Service desk agent Answers employees, fulfills catalog requests and resolves common incidents. It starts in copilot mode and moves to autopilot one category at a time. L1–L4 5 tasks Ch 17.3.1
  • Access agent Maps access requests to business roles and runs a cross-system segregation-of-duties check. It grants only in-bundle roles with no conflict. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 17.3.3
  • Incident investigation agent Correlates alerts, investigates causes and runs known fixes from approved runbooks. It verifies recovery and rolls back if health does not return. L1–L3 3 tasks Ch 17.4.1
  • Change agent Schedules and runs standard changes in their window. It drafts records, risk assessments, test evidence and back-out plans for other changes. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 17.4.2
  • Batch and interface operations agent Diagnoses failed batch jobs and interface messages across a mixed estate. It restarts or reprocesses only allowlisted, idempotent work. L1–L3 6 tasks Ch 17.5.1
  • Release test agent Maps release notes to configurations, generates tests for affected flows and runs them in the sandbox. A release manager decides go or no-go. L1–L3 2 tasks Ch 17.5.3
  • Employee front-door agent One conversational entry for IT, HR and finance questions. It routes each to the right domain agent. Level not stated 1 task Ch 17.7.2

Tax, trade and statutory reporting

4 agents

Agents prepare and explain. Engines decide every number. People sign every filing. Book, Ch 18

  • Indirect tax agent Finds master-data errors behind indirect tax, chases certificates and prepares returns. The tax engine decides every number. L0–L4 7 tasks Ch 18.2.1
  • E-invoice agent Pre-validates outbound invoices against country schemas and triages clearance rejections. It prepares resubmissions changing only allow-listed fields. L2–L4 5 tasks Ch 18.4.3
  • Trade agent (AG-LOG-004) Proposes tariff and export classifications and rolls up origin. It builds broker data packs and clears screening false positives only with evidence. L1–L3 8 tasks Ch 18.2.1
  • Statutory and tax reporting agent Collects data for the tax provision, transfer pricing and local accounts. It drafts and tags; directors and named filers sign. L1–L4 10 tasks Ch 18.2.1

Environment, health and safety

5 agents

Intake, investigations, safety data sheets, permits and regulator reports. Stop-work stays human. Book, Ch 19

  • Incident intake agent Takes incident and near-miss reports in any channel and language. It structures them, proposes a class and can start a regulator clock. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 19.3.2
  • CAPA agent Builds the investigation evidence pack within hours and prompts system-level causes. It drafts corrective actions and checks they worked. L2–L4 5 tasks Ch 19.4.1
  • SDS agent Reads each incoming safety data sheet, extracts its fields and checks it against site inventory. It flags changes that affect labels, storage or training. L1–L3 4 tasks Ch 19.6.1
  • Permit agent Pre-validates permit-to-work requests: workers, contractor, work and conditions. A competent person walks the area and issues the permit. L2 2 tasks Ch 19.7.2
  • EHS report agent Assembles regulator packs and watches permit conditions. It drafts notices; a named person files and signs. L1–L3 5 tasks Ch 19.5.3

Legal, risk and insurance

7 agents

Contracts, obligations, NDAs, entities, legal holds, regulatory change and claims. Book, Ch 20

  • Contract lifecycle agent Drafts contracts from templates and the clause library and routes them by value. One playbook serves procurement and legal. L2 2 tasks Ch 20.2.1
  • Obligation extraction agent Turns signed terms into dated records citing page and clause: notices, renewals, caps and SLAs. L2–L3 2 tasks Ch 20.2.2
  • NDA agent Accepts the company’s own NDA unchanged and redlines third-party NDAs against the playbook. It is the first legal L3 candidate. L2–L3 2 tasks Ch 20.2.3
  • Entity management agent Tracks directors, registered agents and statutory filing calendars. It drafts annual returns and minutes and chases signatures. L2 2 tasks Ch 20.2.3
  • Legal hold and e-discovery agent Identifies custodians and systems, issues hold notices and tracks acknowledgments. It collects and does first-pass review. L1–L2 2 tasks Ch 20.2.4
  • Regulatory change monitor Reads official journals and regulator sites daily. It maps each change to the policies and controls it touches. L1–L2 1 task Ch 20.2.5
  • Claims support agent Assembles trace extracts, reconciles costs and drafts chronologies after an agent incident. It checks proof-of-loss packs against policy conditions. Level not stated 3 tasks Ch 20.8.4

Harness and governance (cross-cutting)

4 agents · 10 human roles

Agents that watch other agents, and the human roles that own, evaluate, operate and stop them. Book, Ch 05, 06, 22, 24, 25

  • Guardian reviewer agent Samples other agents’ outputs and files findings. A guardian may stop, throttle or flag; it may never start, approve, edit or promote. Level not stated 2 tasks Ch 25.3.8
  • Guardian monitor agent Reads traces and observes other agents’ actions. It holds no write tools. Level not stated 1 task Ch 25.3.8
  • Guardian protector agent Calls only the throttle and stop commands of the governance plane. It blocks actions that break limits. Level not stated 1 task Ch 25.3.8
  • Model-as-judge evaluator Grades live outputs so online evaluation is affordable. It is used only after calibration against human graders. Level not stated 1 task Ch 06.5.3
  • Agent business owner Accountable for one agent’s outcomes, limits and risk. A business person, not IT. Can stop the agent. Human role Ch 24.3.2
  • Agent supervisor Runs the daily hand-off queue where agents escalate work to people. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • Agent instruction designer (context engineer) Writes agent instructions, skills and test cases. Works with the process owner on what goes into the context. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • AgentOps analyst Monitors agent health, drift and cost. AgentOps deploys, watches, fixes, changes and retires agents. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • Evaluation engineer Builds test sets, red-teams agents and runs regression. Evals are the gate evidence for promotion. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • AI controls analyst Designs controls over agents and keeps audit evidence. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • AI FinOps analyst Owns meter data, forecasts and showback for agent costs. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • Platform agent specialist Translates enterprise standards into one platform’s agent settings. Never owns agents. Human role Ch 24.3.1
  • Head of the Autonomy Office Chairs the autonomy council, which decides level changes, standards and policy exceptions. The office keeps the register, the plane and the guardians. Human role Ch 25.2.1
  • Kill switch owners The CISO is accountable for the kill switch. Five levels stop an agent version, a tool scope, an identity, a platform or the fleet. Human role Ch 05.8.4

No agent matches these filters.

How far each one is trusted

Autonomy levels, L0 to L5

Levels rate one task, not a whole agent. So one agent can draft at L2 and act alone at L3. Book, Ch 01.5.1

  1. L0 Manual. A person does the work.
  2. L1 Assist. The agent retrieves, drafts and suggests. A person decides.
  3. L2 Approve. The agent prepares the action. A person approves each one.
  4. L3 Act within limits. The agent acts inside limits it cannot change. People handle exceptions and sample.
  5. L4 Run and report. The agent runs the step end to end. People audit and tune.
  6. L5 Full. The agent sets its own sub-goals and limits. A boundary marker, not a target, for financial postings.

An agent may tighten a control on its own authority. Only a person may loosen one. Book, Ch 12.5.3

Raising a level needs evidence and a decision body. Lowering it needs one person and no meeting. Book, Ch 25.2.2 See the scale and who decides.

Finance: record-to-report Book, Ch 12

Close orchestrator agent L3–L4 · Ch 12.3.1

Runs the close calendar across entities. It monitors entity close progress and sequences the close tasks other agents and people perform.

Department
Finance: record-to-report
Autonomy level
L3–L4 across its tasks
Inputs
  • Close calendar
  • Status of every close task
  • Locked local ledgers
Outputs
  • Close status
  • Sequenced tasks and batches

Owner
Agent product owner
Approver
Controller
What moves it up
Entity close monitoring fits L3-L4 because it watches progress and posts nothing.
What moves it down
If the governance plane fails, agents stop and people continue manually.
Cannot
  • Post through a back door; it proposes through a tool
  • Reach the payment release function

Kill switch
Kill-switch conditions are documented and approved before go-live. Fail closed if the governance plane fails.

  • Days to close: 9 to 4 (Meridian target)
  • Days to entity close: 5 to 2
Exception path to a person
Late or failed tasks go to the entity controller.

Journal agent L1–L3 · Ch 12.5.2

Maps a journal request to a known pattern. It reads source data, builds the entry with support and submits it to the ledger’s own checks.

Department
Finance: record-to-report
Autonomy level
L1–L3 across its tasks
Inputs
  • Journal request
  • Source data and support
  • Journal pattern history (12 periods)
Outputs
  • Proposed journal with link to support
  • Decision trace of who asked, what was proposed and what changed
Owner
Agent product owner
Approver
Accountant; controller after the entity close lock
What moves it up
A pattern qualifies if it occurred in 6 of the last 12 periods (J1). L2 to L3 needs six periods above 98% agreement.
What moves it down
A new account combination or a 25% swing forces individual approval (J3).
Cannot
  • Approve, release or accept a difference above tolerance
  • Loosen a control (only a person may)
  • Post directly; the ledger validates and posts
Limits and thresholds
  • Batch approval only if each entry is below 0.5% of entity performance materiality and the batch below 5% (J2)
  • Equity, intercompany investment, tax or suspense journals always need individual approval (J4)
  • Any journal after the close lock needs controller approval (J5)
Kill switch
Drift sends the item type back to L2. A manual fallback runbook is tested at least once a year.
KPIs and evidence
  • Manual journal share: 62% to below 25%
  • Agent agreement rate above 98% for L3 candidates
  • Post-close adjustments below 30
Exception path to a person
Entries outside J2, or with a J3 or J4 trigger, go to individual human approval.
From the book
Ch 12.5.2, Ch 12.5.1, Ch 12.5.3, Ch 12.10.2, Ch 12.10.3, Ch 12.12

  2. L2 Prepare recurring standard journals for batch approval Ch 12.5.1
  3. L2 Prepare template-based variable journals Ch 12.5.1
  4. L2 Propose reclassifications from findings Ch 12.5.1
  5. L1 Assemble data for estimates and judgments a person owns Ch 12.5.1

Clearing agent L1–L3 · Ch 12.6.2

Matches open items with fuzzy references and many-to-many grouping. A confidence score drives whether it clears, proposes or routes.

Department
Finance: record-to-report
Autonomy level
L1–L3 across its tasks
Inputs
  • General ledger open items
  • Historical cleared items
  • Tolerances set by the controller
Outputs
  • Match decisions with confidence
  • Clearing proposals
  • Investigator analysis
Owner
Agent product owner
Approver
AP or AR lead (weekly sample)
What moves it up
Reconciliation has the clearest definition of correct, so it is the best early target for L3.
What moves it down
If more than 1% of sampled automatic clearings are rejected in a week, the item type drops to L2.
Cannot
  • Write off above tolerance 1 automatically, whatever the confidence
  • Write the clearing document; the ledger’s clearing function does
Limits and thresholds
  • Green: confidence 0.97+ and within tolerance 1 (e.g. USD 5)
  • Amber: 0.85 to 0.97 and within tolerance 2 (USD 5-250)
  • Red: below 0.85 or above tolerance 2
Kill switch
The drift check is the kill switch applied to one process.
KPIs and evidence
  • Auto-clear rate: 35% to above 80%
  • Items still cleared next period above 99%
  • Sample error rate below 1%
Exception path to a person
Red-band items go to an investigator with the agent’s analysis.
From the book
Ch 12.6.2, Ch 12.6.1, Ch 12.10.2, Ch 12.12

Tasks and skills, each with its autonomy level

  1. L3 Clear green-band items automatically; daily sample review Ch 12.6.2
  2. L2 Propose amber-band matches for batch approval Ch 12.6.2
  3. L1 Route red-band items to an investigator with analysis Ch 12.6.2
  4. Level not stated Flag items that will not resolve on their own from aging patterns Ch 12.6.1

Accrual agent L1–L2 · Ch 12.7.1

Finds accrual candidates, estimates amounts and applies the written policy. It proposes the batch with method, data and policy reference per line.

Department
Finance: record-to-report
Autonomy level
L1–L2 across its tasks
Inputs
  • Open orders and received-not-invoiced items
  • Contracts with periodic obligations
  • Written accrual policy
Outputs
  • Accrual batch with method per line
  • Back-test of estimate against actual
Owner
Agent product owner
Approver
Controller (approves the batch with method and back-test)
What moves it up
A method moves to batch approval after six periods above 95% accuracy with no miss above line materiality.
What moves it down
An accrual agent is only as good as the written policy it reads.
Cannot
  • Post; a person approves and the ledger posts and schedules the reversal
  • Own judgmental accruals (legal, bonus, warranty)
Limits and thresholds
  • Example policy: accrue services above USD 10,000 where the service period ended and no invoice arrived
Kill switch

  • K5: 60 minutes (any two of CFO, CIO, CISO)
Kill switch
K1 to K3 stop one agent or scope; K4 and K5 stop many.

How this page was built

  • Every agent, task, level, limit and owner comes from the book. Each one cites its chapter and section.
  • Where the book names a task but not its level, the page says “Level not stated”. It does not guess.
  • Where the book names few agents, the page shows only those. Tax and trade has four because the book names four.
  • Product names from the book’s platform examples are left out. Meridian is the book’s worked-example company.
  • Thresholds are the book’s illustrative values. Each company sets its own.
